The Evidence Is Piling Up That Higher Minimum Wages Kill Jobs
It's a price floor, of course it does. It will be really interesting to see how Seattle evolves with a $15/hr minimum wage.

I believe most of the studies that make this claim have only looked at short-term job growth rather than long term employment and quality of life statistics. I'll concede that businesses might decrease hiring if minimum wages go up; however, this behavior is reactionary and doesn't sustain itself as long as the demand for goods & services remains constant (or grows). In the long term, minimum wages help the economy and creates more jobs. Rationale: Increased wages -> More discretionary income/spending power for low-income families -> demand for goods increases -> more is bought/sold-> businesses react to growth by hiring more people
